# Reaction Structure Search

Obsidian desktop plugin for a lab notebook whose reactions are drawn in ChemDraw (`.cdx` or `.cdxml`). It turns the ChemDraw files into a local reaction database with two uses:

1. **Search** the reaction notes by structure or by reaction drawn in Reactio Draw (exact and substructure, reactants, products, whole reactions).
2. **Export** selected reactions as an [Open Reaction Database](https://open-reaction-database.org) (ORD) dataset.
3. **Prepare PubChem deposition files** for the products of a paper (SDF + PubChem CSV), linked to the paper by its DOI.

Everything runs locally with the bundled RDKit.js (no Python, no network).

**Requirements:** Obsidian 1.14 or later (older versions are not tested), desktop only. **Reactio Draw** plugin for drawing the query; **Dataview** for the exports from a Dataview table (a hand-written table of `[[links]]` works without it). The ChemDraw files must be in the *ChemDraw folder* set in the plugin settings — the search and both exports look for them only there.

Atom labels that ChemDraw itself did not interpret are read in this order: BChemLookup entry, a small supplement of common groups that BChemLookup lacks (`shared/cdx/label-grammar.js` in the source repository), then a condensed-formula grammar (`NBpin`, `CH2CH2OH`, `CO2tBu`, `N(iPr)2`, `HO`, `O2N`, `(CH2)3` …). A label that still cannot be read, and generic labels such as R, X or Ar, become "*" — never a carbon: the structure is not an exact hit, a substructure hit shows *label not interpreted*, and the ORD export reports an error. Abbreviations with several attachment points are joined in ChemDraw's stored order; captions stored as atoms (`rt`, `3f`) are ignored.

Chemical abbreviations come from **BChemLookup**, the community-curated abbreviation table of the Beilstein-Institut (CC0), bundled with the plugin: atom labels that ChemDraw itself could not interpret (e.g. `OTr`, `NPhth`, `B(pin)`) are expanded to their structure, and reagents written as text above or below the arrow (`THF`, `K2CO3 (2 equiv)`) are recognised by name — see *Credits*.

## Search
Settings: the folder with the reaction notes and the folder with the ChemDraw files (both default to the vault root).

Start a search with the search button in a Reactio Draw tab (or its command *Search the reaction journal with the current drawing*); the ribbon icon *Search reaction journal* opens Reactio Draw; **Show reaction search results** reopens the last results, **Rebuild reaction search index** rebuilds the index by hand. The dialog starts with *structure*, role *product*, *substructure*, *any stereo* — choose role *reactant*, *any*, *above arrow* or *below arrow* to search elsewhere; a drawing with a reaction arrow is searched as a reaction.

Which ChemDraw file belongs to a note: the file named like the note (`A_141.cdx` for the note `A_141` or `A_141 …`, upper/lower case ignored, the longest matching name wins), else the first `.cdx`/`.cdxml` the note links or embeds.

The results view shows 50 results at a time (**Show more** for the next ones) and the number found at once; a long search shows its progress in the dialog and can be stopped with **Cancel**. Exact search compares the SMILES stored in the index, and substructure search first skips the molecules whose stored RDKit pattern fingerprint cannot contain the query, so a search over thousands of reactions takes seconds (see the timing in the article's Supporting Information).

In the results, tick the notes you want (or **all**), type a tag and press **Add tag**: the tag is added to the `tags` of each picked note (front matter), e.g. to collect the reactions for a paper (`paper-2026`) before an ORD export or a Supporting Information draft. A note with several hits counts once. The index is built automatically in `.reaction-index/`, updated for changed files and rebuilt when a plugin update changes how structures are read. Stereochemistry is read from ChemDraw's wedge and hashed-wedge bonds and the drawn geometry of double bonds (E/Z). By default (**any stereo**) structures are compared by constitution only; in **exact** mode you can choose **relative stereo** (the same configuration as drawn or its mirror image — for racemates) or **absolute stereo** (exactly as drawn). Substructure search always ignores stereochemistry (the bundled RDKit.js has no chirality-aware substructure match). Hydrogens drawn as atoms are made implicit (wedges on them are kept; deuterium, tritium and H2 stay). Reagents written as text next to the arrow are found too if their name is in BChemLookup (role *above/below arrow*); a component drawn as a ChemDraw group (e.g. a salt) is searched as one structure. If `A_141.cdx` and `A_141.cdxml` both exist, only the newer one is used and a warning is shown.

## ORD export
Commands:
- **Export ORD dataset from current table** — in a note with a Dataview query (TABLE or LIST) whose rows link to reaction notes, run through the Dataview API (the first ```` ```dataview ```` block; `dataviewjs` is not supported; the first note link of each row); without a query, the first Markdown table of `[[links]]` in the note is used.
- **Export current note to ORD** — one reaction note.

Settings (section *ORD export*): **Include procedure text** (off by default; can also be switched in the export window, the last choice is kept), author name and **e-mail (both required — without them no record is exported; the e-mail becomes public with the dataset)**, ORCID, organization and city — stored only on this computer, not in the vault —, output folder (default `Export/ORD/`; each export gets its own numbered subfolder `1/`, `2/` …), optional `.pbtxt` output, **Include notebook codes** (off), the default role for other components, and the names of the main note fields if your template uses other names (`Date`, `yield`, `scale`, `state`, `eluent`, `Name`, `temperature`, `time`, `atmosphere`, `roles`, `Procedure`, `solvent`, `frequency`, `Mass_Ionization`; the NMR/HRMS fields and `num_in_article` have fixed names; the `Name` setting is also used by the PubChem export).

The export window asks for the dataset name (the file name; default: the note name), a description (required) and optionally the paper DOI and URL. Notebook codes (the ChemDraw file name and the note name, e.g. `IM_1`) are not written; switch on *Include notebook codes* if you want them in the dataset (`provenance.reaction_metadata`, optional in ORD).

What is exported, per note:
| Source | ORD |
|---|---|
| ChemDraw file of the note (`A_141` for note "A_141 …", else the file the note embeds); single-step schemes only | reaction inputs and products as SMILES with the stereochemistry drawn (wedges, E/Z); the details of a product's SMILES identifier say how its drawn stereocentres are meant, from its `Name::`: *racemic mixture* for `rac-`, `(±)` or descriptors such as `(6bSR,10aRS)`; *relative configuration, absolute configuration unknown* for `rel-` (not called racemic); otherwise *absolute configuration as drawn* (a name marking rac-/rel- on a drawing without stereocentres is a warning) (RDKit must be able to sanitize the structure; generic R/X/Ar are errors) |
| ChemDraw reagent table (matched to the structures by ChemDraw's component reference; no table, or a drawn component without an amount, is an error) | amounts as shown (mass, moles, volume; solutions by moles, listed solvents by volume), and the other shown values as compound features (mass, volume, molarity — for solvents no molarity, and a mass only with a density); reagents that Reactio Draw keeps in its table from a name written as text (all values from the table; a name without a known structure, such as MeMgBr, by name and formula; the solvent of a solution as a second component); columns without a structure reference matched by formula (a salt Reactio Draw splits into cation and anion is one compound `cation.anion`); limiting reagent, isolated mass, purity |
| Text above/below the arrow, e.g. `Et3N (2 equiv), THF (2 mL), rt` | names found in BChemLookup become inputs (SMILES + name; the SMILES identifier says it comes from BChemLookup) with the amount written next to them — mL, mg, mmol, or equiv / mol % × `scale::` (mmol); a name without an amount, or not in the table, is a warning and is not exported; conditions such as `rt`, `0 °C`, `12 h`, `N2` are skipped (use the note fields) |
| `yield::` (`82%`, `0`, `n.r.`, `no reaction`, `decomposition`, `not observed`, `traces`; `n.d.` = not determined) | product YIELD; failed reactions are exported; empty `yield::` → the yield of the ChemDraw reagent table, if shown; `n.d.` → no yield (warning) |
| `temperature::` (`25 °C`, `-78 °C`, `rt`, `reflux`; a range is kept as text), `time::` (`16 h`, `30 min`; `overnight` is not read — warning), `atmosphere::` (`Ar`, `N2`, `air`) | conditions, reaction time; a missing or empty field is taken from the reaction file (its *Temperature / Time / Atmosphere* caption, else the Reactio Draw record; the export report names the source); with no value anywhere nothing is written (no room temperature, air or ambient pressure is assumed) and the report lists it as *not recorded* |
| `Date::` (a date in the future is an error), `scale::` (warning if it differs from the limiting reagent by more than 5 %), `state::`, `eluent::`, `Name::` (only when the scheme has one product; the first product is the desired one and carries yield, mass and purity), NMR and HRMS fields, `solvent::`/`frequency::` (NMR), `Mass_Ionization::`, section **Procedure** (only if *Include procedure text* is on) | provenance, colour/texture, purification workup, product name, analyses, procedure text. `eluent::` (with an optional `workup::` or `purification::` text) becomes a workup step: FLASH_CHROMATOGRAPHY only when that text says chromatography (`workup:: flash chromatography on silica gel`), otherwise a CUSTOM step with the text (`workup:: flash filtration through Al2O3` → *flash filtration through Al2O3; eluent: …*). The order of addition is not recorded in the notes, so no `addition_order` is written. A field the record is built from that is written on more than one line of the note is an error: the record is exported only as a draft, and the draft leaves that field out, with everything that follows from it (no yield, name, stereo details or condition taken from elsewhere in its place) |

Roles: products are right of the arrow; for the rest, the first rule that matches wins — `roles::` line in the note (e.g. `roles:: MeMgBr = reagent; Pd(PPh3)4 = catalyst; THF = solvent` — names as the export report lists them: the label on the scheme, else the name in the solvent list, else the formula from the reagent table, else `structure <id>`; `reactant 1`, `reactant 2` … left to right are also accepted; roles reactant, reagent, catalyst, solvent, unspecified, workup; separated by `;` or new lines; a name that is none of these but is in the plugin's list of common reagents or BChemLookup is matched by its structure; `workup` marks a quench or other addition after the reaction, e.g. `roles:: MeMgBr = reactant; C6H8O7 = workup` for the citric acid of IM_1: such a component is not a reaction input but a workup step ADDITION with role WORKUP, written before the chromatography step from `eluent::`; the limiting reagent cannot be workup) → **the role chosen in the reagent table of Reactio Draw** (files saved by Reactio Draw keep it; *catalyst* and *solvent* are taken as they are; *reactant* is Reactio Draw's default and has no reagent counterpart, so for it the rules below decide; ChemDraw files and older files have no roles and use the rules alone) → listed solvent given as a volume → transition-metal compound at ≤ 0.2 equiv (catalyst) → limiting reagent (reactant) → its skeleton without leaving groups is found in the product (reactant) → default role (setting *Default role*, reagent unless changed). The lists are in `src/ord/roles.js` of the source repository.

After the export a report lists ✅ exported, ⚠️ exported with warnings, ❌ not exported (with the reason and the assigned roles). **Export anyway as draft** writes every record that could be built (not the notes without a ChemDraw file, reaction arrow or product, nor multi-step schemes) to `<name>_draft.json` next to the export, for completion in the ORD editor. Files are never overwritten.

Submitting: validate the file with `ord-schema` (see `ORD.md` in this folder), then follow the ORD submission instructions (pull request to `open-reaction-database/ord-data`).

## PubChem export
Deposits the compounds of a paper in [PubChem](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov) as substances linked to the paper's DOI. The plugin only writes files; you upload them yourself.

- **Account:** registering in PubChem Submissions gives a *test account* (upload, validate and preview; nothing becomes public). To deposit, request the upgrade to a full account (data-source name, organization, contact); PubChem staff approve it.
- **Start** like Chemistry Word Report: **Export products to PubChem from current table** in a note with a Dataview table (or a table of `[[links]]`) of reaction notes, or **Export products of current note to PubChem** in one reaction note. Only the **products** of the schemes are exported (all steps of a file; P1, P2 … left to right); reactants, reagents and solvents are not.
- **Dialog:** paper DOI (required; a `https://doi.org/…` link is shortened), PubMed ID (optional), *Hold until* (optional, at most one year ahead — records stay private until then), registry-ID prefix (1–20 ASCII letters or digits, e.g. a lab code; also in Settings → *PubChem export*). A draft table shows every product: ✅ ready, ⚠️ warning (no `Name::`, name converted to ASCII or characters removed, racemate or `rel-`, some stereocentres undefined while others are drawn, several products with one `Name::`), ❌ not exportable (no `num_in_article::`, a compound number given to two different structures, R/X/unread label, RDKit cannot read the structure, no InChI, no ChemDraw file, reaction arrow or product). Untick rows to leave them out; **Copy table** copies it as TSV. The inputs are remembered per note.
- **Records:** `PUBCHEM_EXT_DATASOURCE_REGID` = `<prefix>-<paper>-<compound number>` (e.g. `LAB-jacs.6c08636-4a` from DOI 10.1021/jacs.6c08636 and `num_in_article::4a`; PubChem shows it on the record page, and a corrected export with the same IDs replaces the records). Notebook reaction codes are not shown; the older format `<prefix>-<reaction>-P<n>` (`LAB-IM_1-P1`) can be chosen in Settings → *PubChem export* → *Registry IDs*. A note with several products needs one number per product, in the order of the scheme: `num_in_article::4a, 4b` (otherwise only the first product can be exported); characters other than letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-` become `_` in the ID. Other tags: `PUBCHEM_SUBSTANCE_SYNONYM` = `Name::` in ASCII, `PUBCHEM_DOI`, `PUBCHEM_PUBMED_ID`, `PUBCHEM_HOLD_UNTIL_DATE`, `PUBCHEM_SUBSTANCE_COMMENT` ("Compound 4a in doi:…"; with the reaction-code format also "Prepared in reaction IM_1."). Structures with the drawn coordinates and wedges (V3000); a product named as a racemate (`rac-`, `(±)`, `(…RS,…SR)`) gets a racemic stereo group (STERAC) and "Racemic." in the comment, one named `rel-` a relative stereo group (STEREL) and "Relative configuration."; the same structure from several notes is one record.
- **Duplicates:** the same structure (InChIKey) with the same stereo meaning — absolute as drawn, racemic (`rac-`), relative (`rel-`), or no stereocentre — the same compound number and the same name is one record, the other notes named in the comment. The standard InChIKey does not tell these meanings apart, so a drawing named plain, `rac-` and `rel-` in three notes gives three records; the same structure and meaning with another compound number or name is kept twice and the conflict listed in the dialog.
- **Files** in a new numbered subfolder for each export, `Export/PubChem/1/`, `2/` … (never overwritten): `<note>_<date>.sdf` (upload this), `_pubchem.csv` (the same records as a PubChem spreadsheet, without the drawn coordinates; exactly one structure per row: `PUBCHEM_EXT_DATASOURCE_SMILES`, or for a racemate or `rel-` compound `PUBCHEM_EXT_DATASOURCE_INCHI` with a non-standard InChI ending in `/s3` (racemic) or `/s2` (relative) and no SMILES — PubChem lists SMILES, InChI and CID as its structure tags and its own example deposits a non-standard `InChI=1/…`; the `.sdf` stays the preferred upload because it keeps the drawn coordinates), `_structures.tsv` (for checking and the SI: id, inchi_key, smiles, molecular_formula, inchi, iupac_name, extended_smiles, compound_number, note, doi) and `_report.txt`.
- **Upload:** PubChem Submissions → New Submission → Substances → upload the `.sdf` → check the preview (structure, name, DOI, hold date) → commit. To change or withdraw deposited records, upload a corrected export with the same registry IDs, or use **Modify** / **Revoke** under *Substances → Substances In PubChem* in PubChem Submissions.
- Not yet checked on PubChem itself: how PubChem shows the racemic stereo group of the `.sdf`, and how the `/s3` InChI of the `_pubchem.csv` appears on the record and its linked Compound — try both once with the test account; also that the V3000 molfile of the `.sdf` is accepted (PubChem's examples are V2000).

## Network, files and accounts
None needed: everything runs locally with the bundled RDKit.js, no network requests are made and no account is needed. The plugin reads the reaction files and notes of the vault, keeps its search index in the vault (`.reaction-index/reaction-index-js.json`) and writes the ORD and PubChem exports into vault folders (`Export/ORD`, `Export/PubChem` by default). The PubChem files are only prepared: you upload them to PubChem yourself.

## Building
In the source repository, `node build.mjs` bundles `src/`, `src/vendor/rdkit.js` and the shared modules in `../shared/` into `main.js` (no npm dependencies; needs `../tools/bundle.mjs`).

The tests are in the plugin's source repository (with the sources and fixtures; it will be published on GitHub soon), not in the vault's plugin folder. Tests (`<vault>` is the published example vault *Chemistry Lab Notebook*; nothing is written into it): `node tests/search.test.js "<vault>"` — the 23 functional search queries of `../validation/03_functional_search_tests/` on a build made from the current `src/`; `node tests/examples.test.js "<vault>"` — the ORD dataset and report and the PubChem SDF, CSV and report of the example notes, compared byte for byte with the vault's `docs/examples/`; `node tests/ord.test.js "<vault>"` — ORD export rules (roles and the workup role, conditions only when recorded, fields written twice, `n.d.` yield, procedure opt-in, `rac-`/`rel-` details, a ChemDraw 22 file). Reading and search on 10 000 USPTO-50k reactions, timing and the BChemXtract test corpus: `../validation/` (with its README and checksums) and `../benchmarks/rss-uspto50k/`.

The BChemLookup tables were converted once (commit 1cccb31) into `../shared/cdx/bchemlookup-data.js`, which is the only form used at run time (no network needed); the conversion script is not part of this repository.

## Credits
- **BChemLookup** — community-curated chemical abbreviation table of the Beilstein-Institut, https://github.com/Beilstein-Institut/BChemLookup (commit 1cccb31, CC0 1.0): `abbreviations.smi` (substituent labels) and `reagents.smi` (reagent and solvent names), bundled as data. It is the lookup table of BChemXtract: Bänsch, F.; Rajan, K.; Nietfeld, M. Automated Extraction and FAIRification of Chemical Structures from Scientific Publications. *ChemRxiv* **2026**, DOI [10.26434/chemrxiv.15010166/v1](https://doi.org/10.26434/chemrxiv.15010166/v1). Missing names (e.g. Pd(PPh3)4, Pd/C, CuI) can be added there by pull request.
- The parser was checked on the BChemXtract benchmark corpus (https://github.com/Beilstein-Institut/BChemXtract, `testset/`); scripts and results in `../validation/05_outside_corpus_bchemxtract/`.
